questions.q: Which tool is purpose-built for formatted financial statements like the Income Statement and Balance Sheet?
options: BI Publisher
Smart View Report Packages
Financial Reporting Studio
OTBI dashboards
questions.explain: Financial Reporting Studio (Financial Reporting Web Studio) builds grid-based formatted statements run against GL balances, with a defined point of view.

questions.q: What question does data security answer in Oracle Fusion reporting?
options: Whether the catalog folder exists
Given that a user can open a tool, which rows of data they are actually allowed to see
Whether a report can be scheduled
Which reporting tool a company has purchased
questions.explain: Data security, enforced through mechanisms like data access sets, filters the rows returned once a user is inside a tool they have function access to.

questions.q: What is the difference between Shared Folders and My Folders in the Reports and Analytics catalog?
options: Shared Folders are only for IT administrators
My Folders hold Oracle-seeded content and Shared Folders hold personal content
Shared Folders hold Oracle-seeded and organization-published content; My Folders hold content you personally created or saved
There is no real difference between the two
questions.explain: Shared Folders are visible to everyone with access; My Folders are private to the individual user unless explicitly shared.

questions.q: What visualization tool is specifically associated with Account Groups in the Financial Reporting Center?
options: Pivot table
Sunburst
Gantt chart
Scatter plot
questions.explain: Account Groups are displayed in the Financial Reporting Center using the Sunburst visualization tool.

questions.q: What is the typical first step after starting a new Financial Reporting Studio report?
options: Publishing it to the Financial Reporting Center
Adding a grid, then defining its rows
Setting a password for the report
Deleting the GL balances cube
questions.explain: The build sequence starts with adding a grid and defining rows (what you're reporting on) before columns, point of view, and formatting.

questions.q: What problem does an Account Group solve?
options: It replaces the need for the General Ledger entirely
It gives a user a quick, curated watchlist of specific accounts without building a full formatted statement
It schedules reports to run automatically every night
It secures payroll data from unauthorized users
questions.explain: An Account Group is a lighter-weight alternative to a formal statement when all a user needs is to monitor a handful of chosen accounts.

questions.q: Why can OTBI show an invoice that was entered thirty seconds ago, while a Financial Reporting Studio report tied to a nightly-refreshed cube cannot?
options: OTBI queries live transactional data and application view objects directly, rather than a separately maintained, periodically refreshed cube
OTBI is simply a faster version of the same cube technology
Financial Reporting Studio does not support any form of real-time data
There is no actual difference between the two tools' data freshness
questions.explain: OTBI integrates with the application's own data in real time, while Financial Reporting Studio is bound by the refresh schedule of its underlying cube.

questions.q: Where does a finished OTBI analysis get saved by default?
options: It cannot be saved; it must be rebuilt every time
Directly into Shared Folders, visible to everyone immediately
Typically into the user's own My Folders, until published to Shared Folders for others
Into the Scheduled Processes work area
questions.explain: A saved analysis typically lands in the author's My Folders first; publishing to Shared Folders is a separate, deliberate step.

questions.q: What is the simplest way to share an OTBI analysis with other users?
options: Email the analysis definition file to each user
Move or copy it from My Folders into a Shared Folder in the catalog, where catalog and security permissions control access
Rebuild it manually for every user who needs it
Sharing is not possible for OTBI analyses
questions.explain: Catalog sharing via Shared Folders, layered on function and data security, is the simplest way to make an analysis available to other users.

questions.q: How does this lesson connect forward to Chapter 6 of the course?
options: Chapter 6 repeats the exact same mechanics content
Chapter 6 covers the content/substance of specific reports like Trial Balance and AP/AR aging, building on the mechanics learned in Chapter 4
Chapter 6 is unrelated to BI Publisher reports
Chapter 6 only covers OTBI, not BI Publisher
questions.explain: Chapter 4 taught the mechanics of BI Publisher; Chapter 6 revisits many of the same reports from the perspective of what they mean in a real close process.

questions.q: What format is the final output of a data model, regardless of its underlying sources?
options: A PDF file
An RTF template
XML
A Financial Reporting Studio grid
questions.explain: Whatever the data model's sources and structure, it ultimately produces XML, which is what a template consumes to produce the final laid-out output.

questions.q: What is the typical first step in building a new BI Publisher template?
options: Uploading a finished PDF
Scheduling the report
Getting a sample XML data file from the data model to build the layout against
Deleting the existing data model
questions.explain: The workflow starts by obtaining sample XML, which the template author then maps fields and loops against while designing the layout in Word.

questions.q: In a real close process, why does a team repeatedly refresh the same Smart View workbook rather than each person rebuilding their own version?
options: Rebuilding is actually required by Oracle Fusion
A shared workbook stays the single source of truth; only the underlying numbers change as subledgers close and refresh is clicked
Refreshing deletes the previous period's data permanently
Smart View does not allow more than one refresh per workbook ever
questions.explain: Treating refresh as a team habit keeps one shared workbook current as Payables, Receivables, and GL close in turn, rather than duplicating effort.

questions.q: What are the three possible development phases of a Report Package?
options: Design, build, deploy
Filter, prompt, schedule
Author, review, sign-off
Data model, template, report
questions.explain: A Report Package's development can include an author phase, a review phase, and a sign-off phase, though not every package needs all three.

questions.q: Which Chapter 1 scenario does ad hoc Smart View analysis most directly answer?
options: "Generate 1099 forms and email them automatically every January"
"Give me a dashboard the AP team can check every morning"
"I need the Income Statement formatted the same way it's always been"
"I want to pull GL balances into Excel myself and build my own variance analysis"
questions.explain: Smart View's live, Excel-native pivoting and drilling is exactly the scenario where a user wants to work the numbers themselves in a spreadsheet.

questions.q: What might a large "over 90 days" bucket relative to total payables indicate?
options: Nothing of concern; it is always irrelevant
A cash flow problem, a supplier dispute, or a data problem such as an invoice that should have been paid or cancelled
That the company has too much cash on hand
That the General Ledger is misconfigured
questions.explain: A large balance in the oldest aging bucket can point to several different underlying issues, each requiring a different next action.

questions.q: What is identified as the real skill tested by building a month-end reporting package well?
options: Memorizing every button in Financial Reporting Studio
Knowing the correct sequence — investigate first, reconcile next, publish last — not just knowing how to run each individual report
Only knowing how to use OTBI
Having the fastest internet connection
questions.explain: The lesson emphasizes that sequencing, not the mechanical difficulty of any single report, is what separates a competent consultant from a struggling one.

questions.q: What is the fundamental check performed by a Trial Balance report?
options: That every supplier has been paid
That total debits equal total credits across the accounts included
That the Balance Sheet is formatted correctly
That OTBI subject area access is configured properly
questions.explain: The Trial Balance's core purpose is confirming total debits equal total credits, directly reflecting double-entry bookkeeping.
